claims.text: High mixing entropy enables a uniform elemental distribution in high-entropy-alloy protective coatings.
A uniform elemental distribution promotes dynamic formation of a continuous protective tribolayer during wear.
The protective tribolayer may be an oxide layer or a nanocrystalline layer.
A continuous protective tribolayer reduces friction.
A continuous protective tribolayer reduces material removal.
The initial high-entropy-alloy coatings have a homogeneous, single-phase microstructure.
Selectively removing one or more principal elements reduces the alloy's mixing entropy.
Moderate to high sliding speeds and temperatures are conducive to tribolayer formation.
High mixing entropy facilitates rapid and coherent formation of a protective tribolayer.
The protective tribolayer forms through oxidation and/or dynamic nanocrystallization.
Reducing mixing entropy compromises tribolayer formation and stability.
Compromised tribolayer formation results in higher wear rates.
Full-mixing-entropy coatings will form more robust and continuous tribolayers than reduced-mixing-entropy coatings under otherwise identical wear conditions.
Full-mixing-entropy coatings will have lower wear rates than reduced-mixing-entropy coatings.
Full-mixing-entropy coatings will have lower coefficients of friction than reduced-mixing-entropy coatings.
The proposed mechanism operates under moderate to high loads, speeds, and temperatures that promote active tribolayer formation.
